At 800 °C for 12Al-30Mn-1C the spinodal decomposition involved the entire austenitic volume (Fig. 13(c)); high Mn raises austenite stability so spinodal decomposition becomes more significant and occurs at the expense of cellular transformation.

overall_structure.value: At 800 °C the austenite (γ) grains of 12Al-30Mn-1C were fully spinodally decomposed. Optical microscopy shows strongly contrasted light and dark grains, several showing internal transformation/banding; SEM shows rounded, droplet-like light regions in a darker matrix, consistent with spinodal decomposition. Nano-sized κ-carbides form as agglomerated acicular-like precipitates, the finest and least dense configuration among the three spinodally decomposed alloys examined.

source.reason: Overall microstructure description assembled from the 800 °C-tempered 12Al-30Mn-1C evidence (Fig. 5(d), Fig. 8(e,f)) and the discussion of full spinodal decomposition at high Mn.

unmapped_findings: For 12Al-30Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C, only spinodal decomposition involved the entire austenitic volume (Fig. 13(c)); high manganese raised austenite stability so spinodal decomposition became more significant and occurred at the expense of cellular transformation (block b0110, b0113).

Hardness comparison for 12Al-30Mn1C (Table 5): hot-rolled 324 HV → 800 °C tempered 352 HV; in the discussion the paper notes that thickening of precipitates/low inter-lamellar spacing behaviour means some 800 °C tempered structures kept hardness close to their hot-rolled value rather than being strongly strengthened (blocks b0043, b0048, b0051, b0108).

The conclusions text (block b0122) attributes to 'the chemical composition featuring 12% Al + 30% Mn' the 'most dense and thickest nano-sized cuboidal κ-carbides' combined with 'spinodal decomposition + cellular transformation', which contradicts both Fig. 8(e,f)/the results text (12Al-30Mn-1C = finest, least dense acicular-like κ-carbides, and full spinodal decomposition without cellular transformation) and block b0121 (which attributes the medium-dense thin needle-like κ-carbides to 12% Al + 20% Mn). This internal inconsistency is noted here; the results-section description was used for the structure fields.

Fig. 8(e,f) for 12Al-30Mn-1C at 800 °C (×10,000 and ×30,000) shows agglomerated acicular precipitates surrounding large bright blocky islands, appearing as the finest and least dense acicular carbide network of the three alloys (blocks b0058, b0066).
